newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TNT investor PDFM in no rush to sell.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TNT investor PDFM in no rush to sell.

text.p: Phillips & Drew Funds Management (PDFM) on Monday became the second major shareholder in Australian global transport group TNT Ltd to take a wait-and-see attitude towards the A$2.0 billion takeover bid by Dutch postal and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland.

The head of Far Eastern equities at London-based PDFM, Robin Apps, told Reuters that while the cash offer of A$2.45 per share by KPN would probably succeed, there was always a chance that a rival bidder could emerge.
"It (another bid) is always a possibility," said Apps.

Most analysts have described the KPN offer as generous, but some have speculated that an express freight firm such as U.S.-based Federal Express Corp might still consider a bid as TNT would provide it with a solid European operation.
In TNT's 1995/96 annual report, PDFM is listed behind Bankers Trust Australia as the second largest shareholder.
The ranking, which was current on September 9, showed that PDFM had a stake of 14.0 percent but Apps said PDM had reduced its stake to about 11.5 percent since the KPN bid was announced on October 2.
BT has increased its stake to 19.99 percent from 16.9.
BT said it had purchased more TNT stock as the KPN offer price was at the low end of its valuation.
The investment bank and funds manager would not commit itself to accepting the KPN offer, which raised market speculation that BT might seek another buyer for its strategic stake.

KPN wants 100 percent ownership of TNT, its partner in the GD Express business based in Europe, and has set a minimum acceptance condition of 90 percent for its friendly bid which closes on November 19.
Apps said KPN had a reasonable chance of success.
"I don't think we are as dubious (about the bid) as BT," he said.
"We think that it (the offer price) is satisfactory. It is always possible it could go higher, but we'll see."

Another substantial shareholder in TNT according to the annual report which was released on Monday, J.P. Morgan Investment Management, has reduced its stake in TNT to 6.12 percent or 35.86 million shares from 7.19 percent.
Brokers said J.P. Morgan and PDFM are believed to have sold their shares to KPN which opened a very small sales window for TNT investors on the day of the bid to buy a 9.9 percent stake.

In offer documents released on Monday, the chairmen of TNT and KPN recommended that shareholders approve the offer which was 50 percent higher than they could have received on the day before the offer was announced.
TNT shares ended one cent lower at A$2.40 on Monday on turnover of 1.1 million.
The shares have traded as low at A$1.19 in 1996.
KPN chairman Wim Dik has said the offer was generously priced to ensure that the acquisition was friendly and trouble-free.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
